recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce target or add redundant guidance; if the stale checked-in SVG diagram matters, handle it through normal FHIR diagram regeneration rather than a one-off source reconciliation edit.
issue_request: FHIR-44633 was an Applied/Persuasive InM change request for R6 asking whether MessageHeader.destination.receiver, after gaining Device support in FHIR-43530, duplicated MessageHeader.destination.target; the accepted resolution was to remove MessageHeader.destination.target.
initial_application: Commit 4c124a6cacc5391cd289af86b12d7aa4a4ba5a27, later merged by e9d5c4f11c, deleted the MessageHeader.destination.target element from source/messageheader/structuredefinition-MessageHeader.xml.
additional_context: FHIR-43530 explains why Device remained valid on MessageHeader.destination.receiver. InM minutes from 2024-04-02 record the 4-0-0 motion to remove target after Zulip outreach found no use case. source/fhir.ini records MessageHeader.destination.target under R5-to-R6 changes, which is an expected release-delta record rather than a live element definition; the only other current hit is a generated-looking SVG artifact.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/messageheader/structuredefinition-MessageHeader.xml is build-scoped and already omits destination.target while retaining destination.receiver with Device and other actor targets.
